ledger.note: -63: Albania stands as a kingdom in the eastern Caucasus. The page says only that it 'emerged in the eastern Caucasus in 2nd or 1st century BC' and first appears as a vassal in Tigranes' empire (95-56 BC); -63 is Cliopatria's first shape, bridged (the page is silent on the year).

region.text: the right bank of the Kura up to the Araxes, including Artsakh and Utik

ledger.note: 387: after the partition of Armenia Albania seizes the Armenian right bank of the Kura. 'After the partition of Armenia between Byzantium and Persia (in 387 AD), Albania with Sassanid help was able to seize from Armenia all the right bank of the river Kura up to river Araxes, including Artsakh and Utik.'

region.text: the lowlands added east of the old outline in Cliopatria's 387 shape (48.1-50.2E, 39.2-41.7N); no page names them

ledger.note: 387: Cliopatria's shape grows by 94 cells toward the Caspian (Mil and Mughan plains, Shirvan side). The page's total (about 45,000 km2) fits an enlarged kingdom but names no eastern land; the Balasagan page has the Sasanians take Balasagan from 'their Albanian vassals in the 5th-century (or possibly as early as 387)'. Bridged to Cliopatria's year.

387: the capital passes from Qabala to Partaw (Barda) in Utik. The page says 'After the partition ... moved ... to Partav' (Armenian influence section) but dates the transfer 'In the 5th century' (Geography section); 387 is the first reading, flagged.

mid-460s: Peroz abolishes the Albanian monarchy after Vache II's revolt. 'the Kingdom of Caucasian Albania had been abolished by Peroz after suppressing a revolt by Vache II in the mid-460s'; the page gives no year, so 465 is the middle of the decade. Same state, same colour: the land is unchanged and Albania stays a Sasanian province.
485: Vachagan III is installed as king. 'Albania remained kingless until 485, when Vachagan III (r. 485-510) was installed on the throne'; the kingdom is restored on the same land.

region.text: the whole of Albania after 387 passes to the Sasanian marzbanate of Aghvank (Arran)

ledger.note: 510: the last king, Vachagan III, reigns to 510; Albania becomes a Sasanian province governed by Mihranid princes ('in the 6th century, it was replaced by princes of the Persian or Parthian Mihranid family'). Cliopatria's last shape is 509 and the Sasanian dossier gains the 74,000 km2 in 510. Fix fx-40 (2 Nov 2026), window request R032: the sasanian-empire entry of identity.successors was removed. Rule R2 of the compiler gives a successor every contested cell from its own start year, so the Sasanian Empire (224) took the Albanian kingdom's land in 260-509 from the first Albanian keyframe on, although the Caucasian Albania page (opened 2 Nov 2026) has Albania a vassal that 'retained its monarchy' from 252 ('In 252, Caucasian Albania acknowledged the suzerainty of the Sasanian Empire'), under a Roman protectorate again in 297 ('the treaty of Nisibis stipulated the reestablishment of the Roman protectorate over Caucasian Iberia and Albania'), a kingdom that 'had been abolished by Peroz' in the mid-460s and restored by 'Vachagan III (r. 485-510)', and no sentence on the land passing to Persia in 510. This dissolve and sasanian-empire/ledger/61 (gain, 510) still hand the land over in 510 (Cliopatria's year, confidence 1); only the standing precedence is gone.

wars.name: Pompey's Caucasian campaign (Third Mithridatic War)
wars.outcome: No change of Albanian land on the page: 'In 69-68 BC Lucullus ... approached the borders of Caucasian Albania' and 'After the 66-65 BC wintering Pompey launched the Iberian campaign'.
wars.note: The page does not say what Pompey did in Albania itself; the Kingdom of Iberia page's infobox lists Iberia as a Roman Republic client 65-63 BC.

wars.name: Alan invasions of Albania, Media and Armenia
wars.outcome: Raids with no territorial result: 'between 134 and 136 [the Alans] attacked Albania, Media, and Armenia'; Roman frontier defences reinforced under Antoninus Pius in 140.

wars.name: Sasanian conquest of the Caucasus
wars.outcome: Albania keeps its king as a Sasanian vassal: 'In 252 Caucasian Albania acknowledged the suzerainty of the Sasanian Empire'; 'In 252-253 Caucasian Albania, along with Caucasian Iberia and Greater Armenia, was conquered'.

wars.name: Partition of Armenia (387)

zones.text: the Armenian right bank of the Kura up to the Araxes, including Artsakh and Utik

wars.outcome: Albania, with Sasanian help, seizes the right bank of the Kura from Armenia: it grows 'to about 45,000 km2'.
wars.note: Not a war with fighting dated on the page; the Partition of Armenia (387) article failed to load.

wars.name: Peroz's suppression of the revolt of Vache II
wars.outcome: The monarchy is abolished 'in the mid-460s' and restored in 485 under Vachagan III; no change of land.
wars.note: Years are the page's 'mid-460s' widened to the decade.

certainty.note: No treaty or survey line is dated on the page. The Kura (Armenia-Albania frontier, 'Classical sources are unanimous') and the Caspian shore are natural lines; the Derbent gates are 'traditionally ascribed to the Sassanid Empire' with no date, so the northern frontier stays approximate.

notes:
CLIOPATRIA ROW: nine shapes -63..509, one outline (about 50,100 km2) to 386 and one (about 74,800-75,000 km2) from 387. The page's figures are 23,000 km2 originally and about 45,000 km2 after 387, so the early outline is 2.2 times too large and the later 1.7 times; both are kept (see keyframes) because the page gives no outline.

CORRECTIONS: (1) The 387 gain on the page is the Armenian right bank of the Kura (Artsakh, Utik: the Karabakh region); Cliopatria's 387 step adds the Caspian lowlands instead and no Karabakh, so the post-387 shapes are corrected by adding Karabakh. (2) 260-286 has no Cliopatria shape; the kingdom persisted as a Sasanian vassal (252), so a new keyframe repeats the pre-387 outline.

END AND AFTER: the dossier ends in 510 (Vachagan III's last year on the page; Cliopatria 509; the sasanian-empire dossier gains Albania in 510). The page runs Albania on as a Sasanian province under Mihranid princes, then under the Rashidun, Umayyad and Abbasid caliphates (Mihranids to 821-22); no Cliopatria row draws 510-637, and the Balasagan row (638-646) reuses the 509 outline almost cell for cell (9 cells differ). A gap-filler may want a dossier for the Mihranid principality of Arran (Aghvank) 510-822 and should see the balasagan dossier's note.

PAGES: Partition of Armenia (387) and Peace of Nisibis (298) did not load by those titles (url_not_found); Peace of Nisibis (299) loaded but does not mention Albania. For 252 and the Roman protectorate c. 297 the Albania page is the only source; the vassal tints belong to the sasanian-empire and roman-empire dossiers (the sasanian-empire dossier has Iberia as vassal from 260 but nothing for Albania before 510).

NOT RECORDED: Pompey's 65 BC campaign in Albania (the page only mentions the Iberian campaign), the Hunnic and Khazar raids (628 Khazars invade Albania, after this dossier's end), Derbent (no date).
